_purpose: independently verify docs/data/glyph_map.json, because tools/encode_text.py's own docstring warns that its `roundtrip` check CANNOT do so: it builds both directions from the same map, so any self-consistent but wrong map passes (demonstrated there by rotating glyphs 500-599 by one -- story text visibly broke, yet 35/35 resources still round-tripped)
_method: compare glyph_map's output against two sources that do not derive from it: (a) the 16x16 1bpp font bitmaps in FDOTHER.DAT resource 4, rendered and read directly, and (b) text this project read off the live game screen on 2026-09-07

result_character_names.note: first pass showed 31/32 with id 28 disputed: glyph_map said 達克塞, my transcription from the small rendered image said 逢克塞. Re-rendering that glyph at 8x settles it as 達 -- glyph_map was right and my transcription was wrong. Evidence: docs/figures/glyphmap-id28-zoom-da-not-feng.png. docs/data/fdtxt000_name_table.json corrected.

observed: 索爾死亡米亞斯多德死亡
result_sample_strings.assessment: all read as coherent, contextually correct Chinese (weapons, items, dialogue, spells, shop, chapter, defeat conditions)
live_cross_checks: 風妖精 appears in Sol's spell list read live off the battle screen
道具店 is a town location label read live off the camp screen

conclusion: glyph_map agrees with the font bitmaps and with live on-screen text on every one of the 104 glyphs actually exercised, with zero mismatches once my own transcription error is removed. This is a real independent check, unlike roundtrip. It does NOT cover the remaining 94.3% of entries -- widening it means exercising more strings, not re-running roundtrip.

round2_2026_09_07._why: worklist 659 asks for human proofreading of the 33-chapter transcription. The worklist body itself already records that premise as outdated (decode_story_text.py decodes all 35 FDTXT resources with ZERO unmapped characters), leaving 'spot-check that each glyph id maps to the right character' -- i.e. exactly this verification.

meaningful_denominator.note: glyph_map has 1825 entries; 1792 of them are actually exercised by the game's text

automated_screen.method: render the game's 16x16 1bpp glyph and glyph_map's claimed character in MingLiU at 16px, take the best Jaccard overlap over a small alignment window
automated_screen.positive_control: the 104 already eye-verified glyphs score median 0.483 (min 0.278)
automated_screen.negative_control: pairing each of those glyphs with a DIFFERENT character scores median 0.287 (max 0.440)
automated_screen.honest_limit: the two distributions OVERLAP (correct-min 0.278 < wrong-max 0.440), so this metric is a ranking/triage tool, NOT a decision rule -- the game font and MingLiU are different fonts

eye_check_of_the_worst.brackets: glyphs 558/561 scored lowest of all and were zoomed separately (docs/figures/glyphmap-bracket-zoom-558-561-180.png): the game draws double-stroke corner brackets 『 』 exactly as claimed; the apparent difference is MingLiU thinning them at 16px, not a mapping error. Punctuation scores low simply because it has few pixels.

coverage.reading: 128 glyphs have been read directly against the game's own bitmaps and cover 27.1% of every character occurrence in the game's text. A further 138 high-frequency glyphs were screened by the metric and all scored ABOVE the 24 that were eye-checked and found correct; counting them reaches 75.2%, but they were not individually inspected and should be described that way.
